THE SCHOOL HALL · HALLOWEEN · OCTOBER 31 · AGES 2–5

Halloween — dress up, say boo, print the party.

Boo! Halloween is the night of friendly ghosts, silly pumpkins and costumes everywhere. On this page: what Halloween is, why people celebrate it, party ideas a toddler can join, and thirty-four printable cards — action moves, party activities, ghost feelings and October things to name.

Back to the Hall ↗
WHAT IS HALLOWEEN?

What’s this? Why do we celebrate it?

A long, long time ago, people believed that on the last night of October, silly ghosts and playful goblins came out to visit. Nobody wanted to be scared — so they dressed up in costumes too, lit lanterns and shared treats to keep everything friendly. That’s why Halloween looks the way it does today: we wear costumes, we carve pumpkins with smiling faces, and children knock on doors to say “trick or treat!” and collect a little candy.

Today Halloween is a dress-up party for whole neighborhoods. For a two-year-old that might mean one orange pumpkin to point at; for a five-year-old, a whole costume parade. Nothing here needs to be scary — every monster on our cards is friendly, and the only thing they bite is a cookie.

TRY IT · ACTIVITIES FOR KIDS

Little-kid Halloween, hour by hour.

Scoop a pumpkin with a grown-up and count the seeds. March in a costume parade around the living room. Bob for apples floating in a big bowl — or for the toddler version, fish them out with a spoon. Sort candy by color into cups. Wrap each other in toilet-paper mummies and waddle. Freeze like a zombie when the music stops. Then settle down with a not-scary ghost story and a paper bat to cut and stick.

The activity cards below carry these ideas as pictures — print them, cut them out and let your child pull the evening’s plan out of a party hat, one card at a time.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

After the candy is sorted.

Back to the School Hall · All holidays ↗Make it in the Art Room · Ages 2–5 ↗Big feelings, kindly in Class 38 · Ages 4–5 ↗

When the costumes come off, the Hall’s calendar already knows what’s next — and the ghost feelings cards make a gentle bridge back to everyday feelings: happy, sad, calm, brave. Trick or treat was the practice; naming feelings is the skill.

Keep it friendly. Toddler Halloween is orange food, one costume and five silly monsters — the cards below are exactly that, and every one prints free.
